rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created human beings with a sound nature, awareness of good and evil, and an inclination to choose good and avoid evil.
rows.anchor: God has created man in the best of moulds with the best of natures. He has granted him the awareness of good and evil

rows.speaker: philosophers
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the philosophers’ blank-slate view: environment and tradition do not make human nature from scratch.
rows.anchor: wrong are the philosophers who say that the nature of a human being is like a clean slate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human moral nature is not animal instinct; free will lets people pursue desires and worldly love despite knowing right from wrong, even inventing excuses.
rows.anchor: a person has the power of free will as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic guidance is needed because human weakness can mislead people despite their moral awareness, and they cannot grasp every consequence of innate concepts.
rows.anchor: a person is in need of prophetic guidance not because he did not have an awareness of good and evil in him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets teach principles rooted in human nature, so upright people recognize their message inwardly while people with corrupted natures oppose it despite inward assent.
rows.anchor: all upright people regarded the calls of the prophets to the calls of their own self

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is called dhikr because it recalls innate truths people forget and neglect.
rows.anchor: it reminds people of the concepts already found in them but they kept forgetting them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “lā tabdīla li-khalq Allāh,” lā negates permissibility, not existence, possibility, or occurrence: changing God’s created nature is impermissible.
rows.anchor: the particle َلَا is not meant for negation or negation of a possibility or negation of happening. Here it refers to negation of permissibility

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows the purpose of His creatures; trying to improve His design, like repositioning eyes or reversing sex, is absurd and bound to fail.
rows.anchor: It is much like placing the eyes that God has placed near the forehead at the back of the neck

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the religion of human nature means leaving the straight path and ruining worldly and religious life, even when deviation is dressed in scientific claims.
rows.anchor: his worldly and religious life will be ruined even if this deviation is made with the help of tall claims from science

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion of nature is the upright religion because it directly accords with human intellect and nature and provides a straight, short route to God.
rows.anchor: it is this religion which has direct relationship with a person’s intellect and nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people fail to recognize this truth, distort the religion, and then work to preserve and promote the distortion.
rows.anchor: most people are not aware of this reality. For this reason they have distorted it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is singular in wording but plural in implication: the Prophet is addressed as Muslim advocate and leader, and the plural circumstantial expression confirms this.
rows.anchor: The plural nature of the accusative of state confirms this deduction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding call to devote themselves to God, the next verse commands the Prophet and Muslims to turn to God, fear Him, and keep within His limits.
rows.anchor: The earlier verse asked the Prophet (sws) and as a result all Muslims to dedicate and devote themselves to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is a basic directive of the religion, protecting and manifesting dedication to God, turning to Him, and God-consciousness.
rows.anchor: It is not only the protector but also the manifestation of dedication to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to avoid idolaters is an admonition to keep away from those who have ruined the implications of the upright religion.
rows.anchor: they should remain at a distance from the Idolaters because they have ruined all the implications of this upright religion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says the Muslims are addressed instead because obstinate polytheists are treated as unworthy of direct address.
rows.anchor: the polytheists are not worthy of being addressed because of their stubbornness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslims were warned away from polytheism as an expression of abhorrence, not because they might join idolaters; the obstinate idolaters are bypassed as unworthy addressees.
rows.anchor: this is an expression of abhorrence from polytheism and polytheists and has been stated while addressing the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In distress idolaters humbly call on God, but after receiving mercy they forget Him and return to the deities they associate with Him.
rows.anchor: when they are caught in a whirlpool, they beseech God with humility and obedience but when God blesses them with His mercy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern of turning to God in hardship and reverting to association after relief has appeared in earlier forms and recurs at Luqman 31:32.
rows.anchor: This subject has been discussed earlier in various styles and is also coming up in verse 32 of Sūrah al-Luqmān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s ingratitude theme recalls al-‘Ankabūt 29:66, where people receive God’s favors but thank others.
rows.anchor: they receive favours from God but thank others and in this way show ingratitude to His favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite their ingratitude, the idolaters may enjoy God’s favors temporarily, but they will soon face the consequences.
rows.anchor: in spite of their ingratitude they may benefit from God’s favours but soon they will bear the consequences

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative suppresses part of the discourse, recoverable from the speaker’s tone: either they invented partners without basis, or God revealed proof for them.
rows.anchor: a part of the discourse is suppressed in such interrogative sentences. It can be gauged from the tone of the speaker

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suppressed question carries sarcasm, humiliation, anger, and wrath; the Qur’an’s final group contains subtle examples of this style.
rows.anchor: sarcasm and humiliation, anger and wrath all are encapsulated

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A psychological argument for monotheism is that helpless people abandon other means and invented deities and turn wholeheartedly to God, then revert to misconduct when relieved.
rows.anchor: when a person is really in need and is helpless, he leaves all other means and sources as well as his self-invented deities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their return to associated deities after receiving mercy shows that temporary reliance on God has not displaced habitual polytheism.
rows.anchor: when God blesses them with His mercy, they forget God and return to their deities whom they associate with Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expects people to be grateful for favors and patient through trials brought by their misdeeds, although few manage either response.
rows.anchor: the Almighty wants people whom He blessed with favours to be grateful. Similarly, He wants them to show patience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people become arrogant when favored and despair when afflicted; the general observation directly warned the Quraysh about their present arrogance and future seizure.
rows.anchor: at the time of revelation of this sūrah, they obviously referred to the Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calamities caused by people’s misdeeds follow God’s established practice for evil people, while prophets such as Abraham also undergo trials under a separate divine testing practice.
rows.anchor: in this world all people even the great prophet Abraham (sws) undergo big trials

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good people’s trials need not result from their deeds; often God uses them to train and improve people.
rows.anchor: in most circumstances it is because God wants to train and improve people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone controls the increase or decrease of sustenance, and His choice is based on wisdom.
rows.anchor: abundance or constriction in sustenance is in the hands of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since provision rests with God, neither despair nor pride is warranted; people should be grateful for favors and patient in trials.
rows.anchor: For this reason, neither is it permissible for anyone to despair nor show pride and conceit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests people through both abundance and hardship, and only the Hereafter will reveal who passed the test.
rows.anchor: It will only be in the Hereafter when we will come to know who succeeded in this test and who failed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A first sign of faith is that God controls every affair of the universe, including sustenance just as He controls life and death.
rows.anchor: all the affairs of this universe are in the control of God, the one and only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second sign is that abundant or scant worldly provision does not indicate success or failure; both conditions test people, with judgment deferred to the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: neither is an abundance of sustenance in this world an indication of a person’s success nor its scantiness an indication of a person’s failure

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third sign is that gratitude and patience are constant trials and the source of a person’s higher qualities; Islahi explains this elsewhere in his exegesis.
rows.anchor: The fountainhead of all higher qualities in a person is these two traits

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After naming prayer as the foremost pillar of the religion of nature and warning against conceit over wealth, the discourse explains how gratitude should be expressed.
rows.anchor: Earlier in verse 31, the foremost pillar of this religion of nature has been mentioned in the form of the prayer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those blessed with wealth owe a rightful share to kin, the destitute, and travelers; they are entrusted to fulfill it, and neglect makes them usurpers.
rows.anchor: there is a rightful share in the wealth of a person who is blessed with means and resources by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving to please God is the right path and leads to success in the Hereafter; using wealth for conceit, luxury, and greed leads to loss before God.
rows.anchor: people who make their wealth to be a means of conceit, luxury and greed will find that this wealth will become a means of loss and failure before God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribā names both money lent at interest and the interest charged; Islahi rejects the gloss “gift” and explains it as naming something by its consequence, citing Yūsuf 12:36 and his essay.
rows.anchor: Those who regard it to mean a gift are absolutely wrong. This word is used in accordance with the linguistic principle of Arabic

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here zakāh is not a technical term but means charity (ṣadaqāt), a usage found elsewhere in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: The word ٍةو ٰکَز here does not occur here as a term. It refers to charity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse contrasts the prior call to give: interest-based lending extracts from others and does not grow with God, whereas wealth spent to please God does.
rows.anchor: Only that wealth increases with God which is spent in His way to please Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi likens interest wealth to an ox fattened by grazing on others’ land; it lacks blessing, unlike earnings from one’s own field spent to fulfill rights and please God.
rows.anchor: God has compared the wealth of an interest-charger to an ox that grows fat by grazing on the lands of others

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rate at which wealth given in God’s way increases is detailed elsewhere in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: The rate of this increase has been mentioned in detail at another instance in the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of the future drives wealth accumulation, but people see only their worldly future and miss the Hereafter; investing with God secures wealth for eternal life.
rows.anchor: He is not able to see the real future which is the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permissible business capital grows within its own risky investment, whereas a moneylender hides like an ambush and profitably draws from the needy without taking risks.
rows.anchor: the capital of a tradesman or a businessman after braving many dangers and different circumstances increases from its own circle of investment
